question: C++ is an example of which type of computer language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Object-Oriented Language.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C++ was developed by Bjarne Stroustrup at Bell Labs in 1979 (originally called "C with Classes") as an extension of the C language. (वस्तु-उन्मुख भाषा — object-oriented language)

 

• It supports the core pillars of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP): encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction, organising code around classes and objects rather than just procedures.

 

• C++ also retains procedural features from C, but its defining design principle — and the reason it is used to teach OOP — is the object-oriented paradigm.

 

• Other well-known object-oriented languages include Java, Python, C# and Smalltalk.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• C++ is widely used in system/application software, game engines, operating systems and competitive programming due to its performance and OOP capabilities.

 

• The four pillars of OOP (encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism) are commonly tested together with language examples like C++ and Java.

 

NOTE

 

• Visual Programming Language (Option 1): Languages such as Scratch and LabVIEW let users build programs by manipulating graphical elements rather than writing text-based code.

 

• Business Data Processing (Option 3): COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) was specifically designed for business, finance and administrative data processing.

 

• String and List Processing (Option 4): LISP and SNOBOL are examples of languages designed primarily for string and list/symbolic processing.

question: Market Based Economic Dispatch (MBED) Mechanism is related with which of the following ministry?
option_4: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Power.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Market Based Economic Dispatch (MBED) is a power-sector reform mechanism proposed by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC), which functions under the Ministry of Power. (विद्युत मंत्रालय — Ministry of Power)

 

• MBED aims to dispatch electricity generation across the country on the basis of economic merit order (least-cost basis) rather than state-wise scheduling, so that cheaper power is used first nationally.

 

• The objective is to reduce the overall cost of power procurement, optimise the use of generating capacity, and support integration of renewable energy into the grid.

 

• It is implemented through power exchanges and is closely linked to India's broader push for a unified national electricity market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CERC regulates the inter-state transmission and tariff of electricity and functions as a key regulatory body under the Ministry of Power.

 

• Related reforms in the power sector include the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the push toward a "One Nation, One Grid, One Frequency, One Price" market.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Option 2): Administers company law and corporate governance (e.g., the Companies Act); unrelated to power dispatch.

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 3): Handles fiscal policy, taxation and the Union Budget, not electricity dispatch mechanisms.

 

• Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Option 4): Deals with policy and schemes for MSMEs, not power-sector dispatch.

question: Which country won the Men's Asia Cup 2022 for cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Lanka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Men's Asia Cup 2022 (played in T20 format) was held in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in August–September 2022. (एशिया कप 2022 — श्रीलंका विजेता)

 

• Sri Lanka defeated Pakistan in the final to win the title, completing a remarkable turnaround after having lost their opening match of the tournament.

 

• Bhanuka Rajapaksa was named Player of the Match in the final, while Mohammad Rizwan of Pakistan was named Player of the Tournament.

 

• This was Sri Lanka's sixth Asia Cup title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) and is contested among Asian cricketing nations.

 

• India, the defending champion at the time, was eliminated in the Super Four stage of the 2022 edition.

 

NOTE

 

• Bangladesh (Option 2): Did not reach the final of the 2022 Asia Cup.

 

• India (Option 3): Was eliminated in the Super Four stage and did not make the final.

 

• Pakistan (Option 4): Reached the final but lost to Sri Lanka.

question: Which among the following lakes connects the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hussain Sagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hussain Sagar is a heart-shaped artificial lake built in 1562 CE by Hussain Shah Wali during the reign of Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah. (हुसैन सागर झील — हैदराबाद और सिकंदराबाद को जोड़ती है)

 

• It is located between the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad in Telangana and connects them.

 

• The lake is famous for the monolithic statue of Gautam Buddha, installed on the Rock of Gibraltar island in the middle of the lake.

 

• It was originally built on a tributary of the Musi River to supply water and now serves as a major recreational and landmark water body of Hyderabad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hyderabad, founded by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591, and Secunderabad, developed by the British as a cantonment town, together form the twin cities.

 

• Other notable Hyderabad water bodies include Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar, built on the Musi river for flood control and water supply.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanwar (Option 1): Kabartal (Kanwar) Lake is a Ramsar wetland site located in Bihar, not near Hyderabad.

 

• Salim Ali (Option 2): Salim Ali Lake is a small lake located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra.

 

• Periyar (Option 4): Periyar Lake is an artificial lake in the Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala.

question: Personal income of households can be calculated in which of the following ways?
option_1: National income + Undistributed profits – Net interest payments – Corporate tax + Transfer payments from the government and firms
option_2: National income – Undistributed profits – Net interest payments – Corporate tax + Transfer payments from the government and firms
option_3: National income – Undistributed profits + Net interest payments – Corporate tax – Transfer payments from the government and firms
option_4: National income – Undistributed profits – Net interest payments – Corporate tax – Transfer payments from the government and firms
solution_text:
The correct answer is National income – Undistributed profits – Net interest payments – Corporate tax + Transfer payments from the government and firms.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Personal Income (PI) is the total income actually received by households and non-corporate businesses, which differs from National Income (NI) because some income earned is never paid out to households, and some income received is not currently earned. (व्यक्तिगत आय — घरेलू क्षेत्र को प्राप्त कुल आय)

 

• From National Income, we subtract items that are earned but not actually received by households: Undistributed (retained) profits, Net interest payments made by households to businesses, and Corporate tax paid by firms to the government.

 

• We then add Transfer payments (such as pensions, scholarships and subsidies) received by households from the government and firms, since these are received but not earned as part of current production.

 

• This gives the identity: PI = NI – Undistributed profits – Net interest payments – Corporate tax + Transfer payments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Personal Disposable Income (PDI) is obtained by further subtracting direct personal taxes and miscellaneous fees/fines from Personal Income: PDI = PI – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments.

 

• National Income (NNP at factor cost) itself is derived from GDP by adjusting for depreciation, net factor income from abroad, and net indirect taxes.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrectly adds undistributed profits instead of subtracting it, which overstates the income actually received by households.

 

• Option 3: Incorrectly adds net interest payments and subtracts transfer payments, reversing the correct signs.

 

• Option 4: Incorrectly subtracts transfer payments instead of adding them, understating personal income.

question: Which of the following earthquake waves are longitudinal waves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P waves.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• P waves (Primary waves) are longitudinal (compressional) waves — particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation, alternately compressing and expanding the medium. (P तरंगें — अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें)

 

• P waves are the fastest of all seismic waves and are therefore the first to be recorded on a seismograph after an earthquake.

 

• They can travel through solids, liquids, and gases, unlike S waves.

 

• S waves (Secondary waves) are transverse waves, moving particles perpendicular to the direction of propagation, and can travel only through solids.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surface waves — Love (L) waves and Rayleigh (R) waves — travel along the Earth's surface and cause the most destruction during earthquakes, though they are slower than body waves (P and S).

 

• The time gap between the arrival of P and S waves at a seismograph station is used to calculate the distance to the earthquake's epicentre.

 

NOTE

 

• L waves (Option 1): Love waves are surface waves that produce a side-to-side (transverse) shearing motion, not longitudinal.

 

• N waves (Option 3): "N waves" is not a standard classification of earthquake waves; it is not a recognised seismic wave type.

 

• S Waves (Option 4): S (Secondary) waves are transverse waves, not longitudinal, and cannot travel through liquids or gases.

question: Who is the author of the book ‘Elephant in the Womb’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalki Koechlin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Elephant in the Womb' is an illustrated book by actress Kalki Koechlin, chronicling her personal journey and reflections through pregnancy. (हाथी गर्भ में — कल्कि कोचलिन की पुस्तक)

 

• The book combines Kalki Koechlin's writing with illustrations, presenting an honest, humorous take on pregnancy and childbirth.

 

• Kalki Koechlin is a French-Indian actress known for films such as *Dev D*, *Margarita with a Straw* and *Gully Boy*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalki Koechlin has been vocal about maternal health and body-positivity, themes reflected in the book.

 

• Several Bollywood personalities have authored books in recent years combining memoir and lifestyle themes, blurring the line between celebrity and literature.

 

NOTE

 

• Twinkle Khanna (Option 1): Author of books like *Mrs Funnybones* and *The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad*, not 'Elephant in the Womb'.

 

• Konkana Sen Sharma (Option 2): An acclaimed actress and director, but not the author of this book.

 

• Farhan Akhtar (Option 4): An actor, director and musician, not associated with authoring this book.

question: In which of the following sports India did NOT win a gold medal in Commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shooting.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shooting was excluded from the sporting programme of the Commonwealth Games 2022 (Birmingham), so India could not win any medal — gold or otherwise — in Shooting at that edition. (निशानेबाजी — 2022 राष्ट्रमंडल खेलों में शामिल नहीं थी)

 

• India won gold in Table Tennis, including the men's team gold and individual gold medals (e.g., Sathiyan Gnanasekaran/Sharath Kamal).

 

• India's women's Lawn Bowls fours team created history by winning India's first-ever gold medal in Lawn Bowls at CWG 2022.

 

• India dominated Weightlifting, winning multiple golds, including from Mirabai Chanu, Jeremy Lalrinnunga and Achinta Sheuli.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The exclusion of shooting from CWG 2022 was controversial in India, as shooting has traditionally been one of India's strongest medal-winning sports at the Commonwealth Games.

 

• India finished 4th on the medal table at CWG 2022 Birmingham with 22 gold medals overall.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 2): India won gold medals in table tennis at CWG 2022, so this is not the correct choice.

 

• Lawn bowls (Option 3): India's women's team won a historic gold in lawn bowls at CWG 2022.

 

• Weightlifting (Option 4): India won several gold medals in weightlifting at CWG 2022.

question: Who has been appointed as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in September 2022?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Lt. Gen Hari Kumar
option_3: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Khand'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/Khand.ttf') format('truetype');} </style>Lt. Gen Vinod G. Khandare (Retired)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lt. Gen Anil Chauhan (Retired).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lt. Gen Anil Chauhan (Retired) was appointed India's second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) on 30 September 2022. (थल सेना जनरल अनिल चौहान — दूसरे रक्षा प्रमुख)

 

• He took over the position after it had remained vacant since December 2021, following the death of India's first CDS, General Bipin Rawat, in a helicopter crash.

 

• Prior to his appointment, Lt. Gen Anil Chauhan had served as the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Eastern Command and later as a Military Adviser in the National Security Council Secretariat.

 

• As CDS, he also functions as the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee and head of the Department of Military Affairs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• General Bipin Rawat was India's first Chief of Defence Staff, appointed on 1 January 2020, a post created to ensure better coordination among the three armed services.

 

• The CDS is a four-star general-equivalent post and acts as the principal military adviser to the Defence Minister.

 

NOTE

 

• Lt. Gen Hari Kumar (Option 1): He served as the Chief of the Naval Staff (Admiral R. Hari Kumar), not the CDS.

 

• Lt. Gen Vinod G. Khandare (Retired) (Option 3): He served as Defence Advisor to the Ministry of Defence, not CDS.

 

• Lt. Gen Manoj Pandey (Option 4): He served as the Chief of the Army Staff, not CDS.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct?
I. Maize requires moderate temperature, rainfall and lots of sunshine.
II. Jute grows well on alluvial soil and requires high temperature, heavy rainfall and humid climate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maize (Zea mays) is a kharif crop that requires moderate temperature (21°C–27°C), moderate rainfall, and plenty of sunshine during its growing season; it is grown across a wide range of soils. (मक्का — खरीफ फसल)

 

• Jute, known as the "Golden Fibre", grows best on fertile alluvial soil in river deltas and requires high temperature (24°C–35°C), heavy rainfall (over 150 cm), and a humid climate.

 

• Both crops are extensively cultivated in the alluvial plains of eastern India — maize across several states, and jute predominantly in West Bengal, Bihar and Assam.

 

• Since both statements correctly describe the respective growing conditions of maize and jute, both are true.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is one of the largest producers of jute in the world, with West Bengal being the leading producer.

 

• Maize is used both as food grain and as fodder, and is also an important raw material for starch, corn oil and ethanol production.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, as both statements are factually accurate.

 

• Only I (Option 2): Incorrect, as statement II about jute is also correct.

 

• Only II (Option 3): Incorrect, as statement I about maize is also correct.

question: Which of the following keyboard shortcut is used to lock the windows screen in Windows 10?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Windows logo key + L.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Windows logo key + L is the standard keyboard shortcut used to instantly lock the screen in Windows operating systems, including Windows 10. (विंडोज लॉगो कुंजी + L — स्क्रीन लॉक करने के लिए)

 

• Pressing this shortcut takes the user to the lock screen, requiring a password/PIN to log back in, without closing any open applications.

 

• It is one of the most commonly used Windows shortcuts for quickly securing a computer when stepping away.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other useful Windows shortcuts include Windows key + D (show desktop), Windows key + E (open File Explorer), and Windows key + R (open Run dialog).

 

• Windows key + M actually minimizes all open windows, unrelated to locking the screen.

 

NOTE

 

• Windows logo key + M (Option 1): Minimizes all open windows; it does not lock the screen.

 

• Windows logo key + K (Option 2): Opens the "Connect" quick action for wireless display/audio devices.

 

• Windows logo key + N (Option 3): Not a standard, universally assigned Windows 10 shortcut for locking the screen.

question: Theme of World Environment Day 2022 is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only One Earth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• World Environment Day 2022, observed on 5 June 2022, was hosted by Sweden with the theme "Only One Earth". (केवल एक पृथ्वी — विश्व पर्यावरण दिवस 2022 की थीम)

 

• The theme "Only One Earth" also marked the 50th anniversary of the 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment, the event that led to the creation of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).

 

• It focused on living sustainably "in harmony with nature", calling for transformative changes through policies and choices toward cleaner, greener lifestyles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Environment Day is coordinated by the UNEP and is celebrated annually since 1974, with a different host country each year.

 

• India hosted World Environment Day in 2018 with the theme "Beat Plastic Pollution".

 

NOTE

 

• Save Environment for Future (Option 2): Not the official UN theme for 2022; a generic phrase, not the designated title.

 

• Ecosystem Restoration (Option 3): This was the theme of World Environment Day 2021, hosted by Pakistan, launching the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration.

 

• Nature is Money (Option 4): Not an official World Environment Day theme.

question: Ganga Dussehra takes place every year on the ______ day of Shukla Paksha of Jyeshtha month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ganga Dussehra is celebrated every year on the Dashami (10th day) of Shukla Paksha in the Hindu month of Jyeshtha (usually falling in May–June). (गंगा दशहरा — ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल पक्ष की दशमी तिथि)

 

• The festival commemorates the descent of the river Ganga from heaven to Earth, believed to have been brought down by the penance of King Bhagiratha.

 

• "Dus-hara" is interpreted as the day that removes "das" (ten) types of sins, and devotees take a holy dip in the Ganga, especially at Haridwar, Varanasi and Rishikesh, on this day.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ganga Dussehra is distinct from Dussehra/Vijayadashami, which falls in Ashwin month and marks the victory of good over evil (Rama's victory over Ravana).

 

• Ganga Saptami, another Ganga-related festival, is celebrated on the seventh day of Shukla Paksha in Vaishakh month.

 

NOTE

 

• 6th (Option 1): Not the correct tithi associated with Ganga Dussehra.

 

• 8th (Option 2): Ashtami is associated with other festivals like Krishna Janmashtami or Durga Ashtami, not Ganga Dussehra.

 

• 12th (Option 4): Dwadashi is not the tithi on which Ganga Dussehra is observed.

question: Which of the following comes under the platyhelminthes classification under the animalia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tapeworm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tapeworm (e.g., *Taenia solium*) belongs to the phylum Platyhelminthes, commonly known as flatworms, characterised by a dorsoventrally flattened, unsegmented (or pseudo-segmented) soft body. (चपटे कृमि — प्लेटीहेल्मिन्थीज संघ)

 

• Platyhelminthes includes free-living and parasitic forms such as planarians, flukes (Fasciola) and tapeworms (Taenia), many of which are endoparasites lacking a true body cavity (coelom).

 

• Tapeworms are endoparasites of the human intestine, absorbing nutrients directly through their body surface as they lack a digestive system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Platyhelminthes are typically triploblastic, acoelomate and bilaterally symmetrical organisms.

 

• Other classic examples of this phylum include Planaria (free-living) and Fasciola hepatica (liver fluke, parasitic).

 

NOTE

 

• Sycon (Option 1): Sycon is a genus of sponges belonging to phylum Porifera, not Platyhelminthes.

 

• Leech (Option 2): Leech belongs to phylum Annelida (segmented worms), class Hirudinea.

 

• Wuchereria (Option 3): Wuchereria bancrofti, the filarial worm causing elephantiasis, belongs to phylum Nematoda (roundworms), not Platyhelminthes.

question: The distance of the Sun from the Earth is about ______ light minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The average distance between the Sun and the Earth is about 150 million kilometres (1 Astronomical Unit). (सूर्य से पृथ्वी की दूरी — लगभग 8 प्रकाश मिनट)

 

• Since light travels at approximately 300,000 km per second, it takes light about 8 minutes and 20 seconds (~8.3 minutes) to travel from the Sun to the Earth.

 

• This is why sunlight observed on Earth actually left the Sun's surface about 8 minutes earlier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A light year is the distance light travels in one year, used to measure distances between stars, while light minutes are useful for measuring distances within the solar system.

 

• The Earth's distance from the Sun defines the Astronomical Unit (AU), a standard unit used in astronomy.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 1): Understates the actual light travel time from the Sun to the Earth.

 

• 4.3 (Option 2): This is close to the time it takes light to travel from the nearest star system, Alpha Centauri, in light years, not the Sun-Earth light-minute distance.

 

• 12 (Option 3): Overstates the actual light travel time from the Sun to the Earth.

question: Which of the following do/does NOT come under state list of 7th schedule of the Indian constitution?
option_1: Relief of the disabled and unemployable
option_2: Burials and burial grounds; cremations and cremation grounds
option_3: Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields
option_4: Pilgrimages, other than pilgrimages to places outside India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains subjects on which only State Legislatures can ordinarily make laws. (राज्य सूची — सातवीं अनुसूची)

 

• "Relief of the disabled and unemployable" (Entry 9), "Burials and burial grounds; cremations and cremation grounds" (Entry 10), and "Pilgrimages, other than pilgrimages to places outside India" (Entry 28) are all genuine entries of the State List.

 

• "Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields", however, is Entry 55 of the Union List (List I), since mines and oilfields are subjects of national economic importance placed under Central Government control.

 

• This makes "Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields" the item that does NOT belong to the State List.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Seventh Schedule divides legislative powers into three lists: the Union List (Centre), the State List (States), and the Concurrent List (both).

 

• "Regulation of mines and mineral development" (Entry 54, Union List) is also a Central subject, reflecting the strategic and economic importance of the mining sector.

 

NOTE

 

• Relief of the disabled and unemployable (Option 1): This is a genuine State List entry (Entry 9), so it is not the correct answer to this "NOT" question.

 

• Burials and burial grounds; cremations and cremation grounds (Option 2): This is a genuine State List entry (Entry 10).

 

• Pilgrimages, other than pilgrimages to places outside India (Option 4): This is a genuine State List entry (Entry 28).

question: In ______, a Subsidiary Alliance system was imposed on Awadh by the British.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1801.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Subsidiary Alliance system, devised by Lord Wellesley (Governor-General, 1798–1805), was imposed on Awadh (Oudh) in 1801. (सहायक संधि — अवध पर 1801 में लागू)

 

• Under this treaty, the Nawab of Awadh, Saadat Ali Khan, was forced to cede nearly half of his territory to the British East India Company and disband much of his own army, accepting a British force instead.

 

• The Subsidiary Alliance required Indian rulers to maintain a British armed contingent at their own expense, surrender control of foreign affairs, and accept a British Resident at their court.

 

• Rulers who signed the alliance included the Nizam of Hyderabad (1798), Mysore (1799), and Awadh (1801), among others.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Awadh was eventually fully annexed by the British in 1856 under Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse/misgovernance pretext, becoming one of the immediate triggers for the Revolt of 1857.

 

• The Subsidiary Alliance system was a key instrument of British expansion in India during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

 

NOTE

 

• 1828 (Option 1): This is the year Lord William Bentinck became Governor-General, not the year of Awadh's Subsidiary Alliance.

 

• 1814 (Option 3): This is closer to the start of the Anglo-Nepalese War (1814–1816), unrelated to Awadh's alliance.

 

• 1809 (Option 4): Not the correct year associated with the Subsidiary Alliance imposed on Awadh.

question: Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Los Angles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Los Angeles, USA, will host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games. (लॉस एंजिल्स — 2028 ग्रीष्मकालीन ओलंपिक की मेज़बानी)

 

• This will be the third time Los Angeles hosts the Summer Olympics, after previously hosting them in 1932 and 1984.

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) made a historic dual award in 2017, simultaneously confirming Paris as host of the 2024 Games and Los Angeles as host of the 2028 Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics, marking its third time hosting the Games (after 1900 and 1924).

 

• The 2032 Summer Olympics have been awarded to Brisbane, Australia.

 

NOTE

 

• Paris (Option 2): Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games, not the 2028 edition.

 

• New York (Option 3): New York has never hosted the Summer Olympics and is not the host for 2028.

 

• Munich (Option 4): Munich hosted the 1972 Summer Olympics but is not the host city for 2028.

question: As the river enters the plain it twists and turns forming large bends known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is meanders.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As a river enters a flat plain, its velocity decreases and it starts to twist and turn, forming large, sinuous bends known as meanders. (नदी विसर्प — मैदानी क्षेत्र में नदी के मोड़)

 

• Meanders develop due to unequal erosion and deposition along the banks — erosion occurs on the outer (concave) bank while deposition happens on the inner (convex) bank.

 

• Over time, a meander loop can become so pronounced that the river cuts across its neck during a flood, isolating the loop and forming an ox-bow lake.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Levees are naturally raised river banks formed by repeated deposition of sediment during floods.

 

• The floodplain is the flat land bordering a river that gets submerged during floods, formed by sediment deposition over time.

 

NOTE

 

• levees (Option 1): These are natural embankments along a river's course, not the winding bends themselves.

 

• ox-bow lake (Option 2): This is the horseshoe-shaped lake formed when a meander gets cut off from the main river, not the bend itself.

 

• floodplain (Option 3): This refers to the flat, low-lying land beside a river prone to flooding, not the twisting bends.

question: What were the primary goals of the five-year plans in India?
option_2: Poverty reduction, Urbanisation, Self-sufficiency and Modernisation
option_3: Social welfare, Self-sufficiency, equity and industrial development
solution_text:
The correct answer is Growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Five-Year Plans, launched under the Planning Commission starting in 1951, were designed around four broad goals: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity. (पंचवर्षीय योजनाएँ — विकास, आधुनिकीकरण, आत्मनिर्भरता, समानता)

 

• Growth refers to increasing the country's capacity to produce goods and services (GDP growth).

 

• Modernisation involves adopting new technology and changing social outlook (e.g., gender equality, diversification of production).

 

• Self-reliance means avoiding dependence on foreign imports for essential goods, while Equity aims at ensuring the benefits of economic prosperity reach the poorer sections of society.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused primarily on agriculture, based on the Harrod-Domar model.

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015, ending the era of formal Five-Year Plans after the Twelfth Plan (2012–17).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Industrialisation, Urbanisation, development and self-reliance): Not the standard formulation of the four goals as given in the NCERT syllabus.

 

• Option 2 (Poverty reduction, Urbanisation, Self-sufficiency and Modernisation): Mixes in terms like urbanisation and poverty reduction that are not part of the standard four goals.

 

• Option 3 (Social welfare, Self-sufficiency, equity and industrial development): Close but does not match the precise standard textbook terms of growth and modernisation.

question: “Living root bridges” is an iconic structure found in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Living root bridges" are iconic structures found in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya, particularly around Cherrapunji (Sohra) and Mawlynnong. (जीवित जड़ पुल — मेघालय)

 

• These bridges are grown by training the aerial roots of the rubber fig tree (Ficus elastica) across rivers and streams, a process that can take 15–30 years to complete.

 

• They are a remarkable example of indigenous bio-engineering by the local Khasi and Jaintia tribal communities, and some of these bridges are over a hundred years old.

 

• The Umshiang Double-Decker Root Bridge near Cherrapunji is one of the most famous examples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meghalaya, whose name means "abode of clouds", is also home to Mawsynram and Cherrapunji, among the wettest places on Earth.

 

• Living root bridges have been proposed for inclusion in the UNESCO World Heritage list.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 2): Known for the Darjeeling hills and tea gardens, not living root bridges.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Known for hill stations and apple orchards, not living root bridges.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Known for tea gardens and the Brahmaputra river, not living root bridges (though it shares proximity to Meghalaya, the bridges themselves are a Meghalaya feature).

question: __________ was the first governor-general of Bengal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Warren Hastings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773 under the Regulating Act of 1773, which reorganised the administration of the East India Company's territories. (वारेन हेस्टिंग्स — बंगाल के प्रथम गवर्नर-जनरल)

 

• Before this Act, the head of Bengal administration was called the "Governor of Bengal"; the Regulating Act upgraded the post to "Governor-General of Bengal" and also set up a Supreme Court at Calcutta.

 

• Warren Hastings held the post from 1773 to 1785 and played a key role in shaping early British administrative and judicial systems in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord William Bentinck later became the first Governor-General of India in 1833, after the Charter Act of 1833 upgraded the Bengal post to cover all British India.

 

• Warren Hastings was impeached in Britain on charges of corruption after his return, though he was ultimately acquitted.

 

NOTE

 

• William Bentinck (Option 2): He became the first Governor-General of India (1833) under the Charter Act of 1833, not the first Governor-General of Bengal.

 

• Charles Metcalfe (Option 3): He served as acting Governor-General of India in 1835–36, known for liberalising the press, but was not the first Governor-General of Bengal.

 

• John Shore (Option 4): He served as Governor-General of Bengal (1793–1798) after Cornwallis, but was not the first.

question: The Garba dance is performed in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Garba is a traditional folk dance that originated in the state of Gujarat, performed predominantly during the festival of Navratri. (गरबा — गुजरात का पारंपरिक लोक नृत्य)

 

• Dancers typically move in concentric circles, often around a central lamp or an image of the goddess Shakti/Amba, performing rhythmic clapping and footwork.

 

• Garba is closely associated with Dandiya Raas, another popular Gujarati folk dance performed with decorated sticks (dandiyas).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In 2023, Garba of Gujarat was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Gujarat include Bhavai and Tippani.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Ghoomar and Phag, not Garba.

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known for classical/folk forms like Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam, not Garba.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): Known for Bhangra and Giddha, not Garba.

question: Which of the following is the correct order of friction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Static > Sliding > Rolling.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Static friction is the friction that must be overcome to start motion between two surfaces at rest, and it is generally the largest of the three types. (स्थैतिक घर्षण > सर्पी घर्षण > लोटनिक घर्षण)

 

• Sliding (kinetic) friction acts once an object is already sliding over a surface and is typically less than static friction but greater than rolling friction.

 

• Rolling friction occurs when an object (like a wheel or ball) rolls over a surface, and it is the smallest of the three because the contact area and relative sliding between surfaces is minimal.

 

• This gives the correct hierarchy: Static friction > Sliding friction > Rolling friction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rolling friction being the smallest is why wheels, ball bearings, and rollers are used to reduce friction in machines and vehicles.

 

• The coefficient of friction depends on the nature of the two surfaces in contact and is largely independent of the apparent area of contact.

 

NOTE

 

• Static > Rolling > Sliding (Option 1): Incorrectly places rolling friction above sliding friction.

 

• Rolling > Static > Sliding (Option 2): Incorrectly places rolling friction as the largest, when it is actually the smallest.

 

• Sliding > Static > Rolling (Option 4): Incorrectly places sliding friction above static friction.

question: Which among the following constitutional amendments of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of Sikkim as a state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 36th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975, inserted Article 371F and made Sikkim the 22nd state of India. (36वाँ संविधान संशोधन — सिक्किम भारत का 22वाँ राज्य बना)

 

• Prior to this, the 35th Amendment Act, 1974, had given Sikkim the status of an "Associate State" of India through Article 2A and the Tenth Schedule.

 

• The 36th Amendment repealed Article 2A and the Tenth Schedule, formally converting Sikkim's status from an associate state to a full-fledged state, following a referendum in which Sikkimese voters favoured merger with India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim merged with India in 1975 after the abolition of the monarchy (Chogyal rule) following a popular referendum.

 

• Article 371F contains special provisions for the state of Sikkim, safeguarding its unique laws and land rights.

 

NOTE

 

• 51st (Option 2): The 51st Amendment Act, 1984, dealt with reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Arunachal Pradesh in the Lok Sabha.

 

• 42nd (Option 3): The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, is known as the "Mini-Constitution", which added the words "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" to the Preamble.

 

• 30th (Option 4): The 30th Amendment Act, 1972, dealt with the pecuniary jurisdiction for Supreme Court appeals in civil cases.
